_rule: toggle-wording-proposals-v1 · wording this lane proposes for a switch, drawn beside what the rail says today. NOT LIVE. A proposal accepted is written into zone.html's TOGGLES and deleted from here, so this file empties as the language is settled and its length is the size of the open question.

masorah.why: the marks the scribes added under the letters. Keep them, require them, or set them aside inside the card. The page never changes.
masorah.note: “the pointing” is the scribal term; “the vowels” is the owner’s own phrase for it (2026-09-19, “turn off the masoretic vowels”). Also drops “Masoretic”, which the row never defines.

sources.why: every dictionary this book’s readings stand on. Turn one off and it is not asked; the card says what that withheld.
sources.note: “sources” is our word for them; a reader knows what a dictionary is. Shorter, and drops the second clause that argued a position.

pairs.why: the scribes wrote one word and read another aloud. Which one the English follows.
pairs.note: “pairs” tells a reader nothing on its own. The why already avoided ketiv/qere, which was right; the label should do the same work.

licence.why: prefer readings a source released under one license. Nothing is hidden; only the order moves.
licence.note: drops “a source the site refuses is not in the catalog to be sorted” — true, but it is us defending ourselves inside the interface rather than telling a reader what the switch does.

names.why: a name can be answered with what it means, or with how it sounds.
names.note: drops “the lattice’s transliteration flag, the corpus lane’s rule”. Both are true and neither is a phrase a reader can hold; the provenance belongs in the record, not the label.

edition.why: this is one manuscript tradition. Another great copy spells about a thousand words differently. Mark where.
edition.note: “MAM” is never expanded anywhere a reader can see it. “edition” also reads like a publisher’s edition rather than a manuscript.
